title: Fixed-anchor criterion for purity from a family of curves
statement: Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and $\iota:\Qlb\simeq\mathbf C$ [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $X_0$ be a nonempty geometrically connected separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme and $\mathcal S$ a nonzero classical lisse $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible; def-weil-finite-type-morphism; def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves; def-wf-fundamental-representation], interpreted with the same local operators in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Fix a closed point $x_*$. Let $\mathscr T$ be any collection of data $(m,C_m,h_m)$, where $m\ge1$, $C_m$ is a smooth geometrically connected affine curve over $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$, and $h_m:C_m\hookrightarrow X_0\times_{k_0}k_m$ is a closed immersion [d-real-setup; def-weil-closed-immersion; def-pc-base-change]. Write $R_m\mathcal S$ for constant restriction followed by immersion pullback [def-dl-a1-constant-extension-data; def-zl-constant-extension-restriction-local-data; def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Assume: (i) for each closed point $x$ of $X_0$, including $x=x_*$, some member has closed points $z_*,z$ over $x_*,x$; (ii) each $R_m\mathcal S$ is punctually pure of some real weight $v_t$; (iii) at every closed $z$ above $x$, with $f=[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]\ge1$, the local eigenvalue multiset is the multiset of $f$th powers at $x$ and $q_z=q_x^f$. Then there exists a unique real $w$ such that $\mathcal S$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$. Every eigenvalue $\alpha$ at $x_*$ is nonzero and satisfies $w=2\log_{q_{x_*}}|\iota(\alpha)|$, independently of $\alpha$, and every supplied weight $v_t$ on a member through $x_*$ equals $w$. More generally, any further curve with a closed point over $x_*$ satisfying (iii) and with pure restriction of weight $v$ has $v=w$. For every closed $x$ and every eigenvalue $\beta$ at $x$, $|\iota(\beta)|=q_x^{w/2}$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-classical-realized-anchor-eigenvalue] to obtain a punctual eigenvalue alpha at the anchor. This step is independent of the family of curves and its weights.

source.place: Paragraph 3: existence of an eigenvalue at the fixed anchor; expanded step 1 of lem-zl-anchored-pure-curve-criterion.

proof.text: For each closed $x$, [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a) makes $\kappa(x)$ finite-dimensional over the finite field $k_0$. A basis of size $d$ identifies its underlying set with $k_0^d$, so $q_x$ is finite. Its distinct elements $0,1$ give $q_x\ge2$. Hence $\log q_x>0$ by [def-wf-positive-real-logarithm]; in particular all logarithmic denominators used below are nonzero. We use $\log_{q_x}a=\log(a)/\log(q_x)$.

source.place: Paragraphs 3-4: positivity of residue cardinalities and logarithmic denominators.

proof.text:
Here is the elementary power calculation, for any one of the given pure restrictions of weight $v$ and a closed $z$ over $x$ of degree $f\ge1$. For each eigenvalue $\beta$ at $x$, hypothesis (iii) and purity [def-weil-punctual-weights] give
$$a^f=(q_x^f)^{v/2},\qquad a=|\iota(\beta)|\ge0.$$
Indeed $\iota$ preserves powers, and multiplicativity of [def-weil-complex-absolute-value] gives $|\iota(\beta^f)|=a^f$. The right side is positive, so $a>0$. By [def-weil-real-power] and [def-wf-positive-real-logarithm], $\log(b^t)=t\log b$ for $b>0$: substitute $b^t=\exp(t\log b)$ into $\log(\exp s)=s$. Applying this identity to both sides gives
$$f\log a=(v/2)f\log q_x,\qquad 2\log_{q_x}a=v.$$
The final equality cancels the positive integer $f$ and the nonzero $\log q_x$. In Lean first obtain a finite Weil presentation of the target sheaf by specializing [lem-wf-common-stage-weil-iterate] to a one-vertex quiver with no arrows. Characteristic polynomials commute with scalar extension, and their roots are exactly the eigenvalues. Thus LocalPower sends each source eigenvalue beta to beta^f at z. Cancel the positive natural power on nonnegative reals to obtain directly a=q_x^(v/2), then apply logb only at the anchor. This is a generic finite-diagram tool and does not replace any part of the unit route.

source.place: Paragraph 3, the eigenvalue-power and residue-cardinality calculation, expanded.

proof.text: Apply (i) with $x=x_*$ and select a member of weight $v_0$ with a closed point over $x_*$. For every anchor eigenvalue $\alpha$, step 3 at that point gives $|\iota(\alpha)|>0$; since $|z|=0$ only for $z=0$ [def-weil-complex-absolute-value] and $\iota$ is a field isomorphism, $\alpha\ne0$. Set $A=|\iota(\alpha_*)|>0$ and $w=2\log_{q_{x_*}}A$. Step 3 at that point gives $w=v_0$. Applying the same calculation on this single member to every anchor eigenvalue $\alpha$ gives $2\log_{q_{x_*}}|\iota(\alpha)|=v_0=w$. This proves the nonvanishing, the anchor formula and its independence of the choice of eigenvalue.

source.place: Paragraph 3: define the common weight at the fixed anchor.

proof.text: Let any supplied member through $x_*$ have pure weight $v_t$. Use $\alpha_*$ and its closed point over $x_*$ in step 3: $v_t=2\log_{q_{x_*}}A=w$. For a further curve in the last assertion, its assumed point over $x_*$, power formula (iii) and purity of weight $v$ give exactly the same equation. Thus $v=w$ as well; no membership in $\mathscr T$ was used in that calculation.

source.place: Paragraph 3: the anchor fixes the weight on every curve, including additional curves.

proof.text: Fix a closed point x and eigenvalue beta. Choose by the covering hypothesis a supplied curve with closed points above both x and the anchor. Step 5 makes its weight w. The norm conclusion a=q_x^(v/2) established in step 3, at its point over x, gives directly norm(iota beta)=q_x^(w/2). Since x and beta were arbitrary, this is exactly SfIsPunctuallyPureOfWeight [def-weil-punctual-weights]. No inverse-logarithm exponentiation is needed.

source.place: Paragraph 4: compare at the other point and conclude global purity.

proof.text: If $w'$ is another punctual purity weight, the existing eigenvalue $\alpha_*$ satisfies $A=q_{x_*}^{w'/2}$ by [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Taking the natural logarithm, using $b^t=\exp(t\log b)$ and $\log(\exp s)=s$ [def-weil-real-power; def-wf-positive-real-logarithm], gives $w'=2\log A/\log q_{x_*}=w$. This proves uniqueness.

source.place: Paragraphs 3-4: logarithmic uniqueness of the global weight.

proof_origin.place: The original seven-step argument: step 1 isolated as the classical anchor-spectrum lemma; the other steps are proved from finite-stage descent, LocalPower, characteristic-polynomial scalar extension and real power cancellation.

tool_uses.why: Its coefficient-field fibre equivalence reflects the zero lisse object and supplies a nonzero finite-dimensional anchor fibre on the connected geometric scheme. This generic lisse-sheaf tool is already a statement dependency of def-wf-fundamental-representation and does not replace the curve/anchor route.

Its finite-residue-field assertion verifies q_x is finite and greater than one for the logarithmic calculation. It is a generic finite-type scheme tool already used by def-weil-local-frobenius-trace; the unit has no replacement for Zariski lemma.
